items.title: 68359_Zutty Singleton oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...And Nappy Lamar, and -- [INTERVIEWER] Nappy Lamar, the banjo player.

ctx.x: Was she playing piano in the band then?

Yes, she was playing piano in the band. Yes, she was playing good. A lot of guys in St. Louis would really brag on Marge, said, good piano player. And like Doc Randall, when I was playing at the Club 47 in California, Doc Randall, he was one of the owners of the place, he was a saxophone player. He's in Las Vegas now. And Nappy Lamar, and --

items.title: 68359_Zutty Singleton oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Nappy Lamare '49. Were these sort of mostly things you were working out of California?

ctx.x: And he had his wife and she was a character also. And they left a beautiful home in California. Talk about a beautiful place. They had servants. Because they had a maid, why when you'd go there, why the maid would open the door. They both went out on the road and they didn't pay the taxes the whole time they were out. They didn't pay, they didn't pay anything. They went back and their home was sold at auction. That's the kind of guy he was.

Well this thing where you've got here Zutty. Galliard Slim '46. Wingy Manone (Wingy Lemone?) '47. Eddie Condon '48. Joe Marsala '48, Nappy Lamare '49. Were these sort of mostly things you were working out of California?
No. Condon (Norman?) was out on the road. He was with Wingy (Wingy?) in California.
